title: Switchover decision log + cooldown runbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for an on-call-friendly switchover decision log + cooldown runbook. Focus: region-level degradation where we need to shift production traffic to a warm standby region without flip-flopping and while preserving user sessions and KV cache effectiveness.

Context / motivation:
- We’ve repeatedly observed brief regional network flaps that cause health-probe jitter and repeated traffic shifts. Flip-flopping between regions creates cache churn, increases latency for end-users, and complicates billing reconciliation.
- Proposed approach: add an explicit cooldown gate+decision log during any automated or manual switchover, with concrete observability checks and roll-back windows.

When to use this doc (triggers):
- Region-level 5xx > 3% sustained for 5m AND control-plane RPC error rates increasing
- 95th pct tail latency > target for >10m and cause traced to region-local infra (not model performance)
- Provider-reported availability event for the region (e.g., AZ/region maintenance impacting network egress)
(If only single-service degradation, use the service-level runbook first)

Decision log template (one-line entries; keep short):
- UTC timestamp | decision-maker (oncall) | trigger metric | action taken | target traffic split | reason/notes | rollback criteria | linked ticket/PR
Example:
- 2025-02-10T18:14Z | maya.chen | region-a 5xx=4.2% 10m | shift 20% -> region-b (gradual weights) | 80/20 | region-a API gateway errors, probes failing | rollback if 5xx trend reverses to <1% for 15m or region-b errors >2% | RED-345

Cooldown gate (key idea):
- After any weight change >= 10% or DNS switch, enter a 15–30 minute cooldown window where automatic re-shifts are suppressed unless a critical threshold is crossed (e.g., complete region outage).
- During cooldown: require explicit human approval to change route again unless metrics show total loss (e.g., control-plane unreachable).
- Rationale: prevents oscillation and gives KV-cache time to amortize.

Traffic shift mechanics (options):
- Weighted routing (preferred for gradual): adjust load-balancer weights in 10% increments every 2 minutes up to target split. Observe error and tail latency after each step.
- DNS TTL reduction + new record: For global DNS providers where weighted routing is not possible. Reduce TTL to 30s only if preplanned. Avoid repeatedly changing TTL.
- Anycast / region-pref: If using anycast, route-change may be best-effort — record provider guidance and expected convergence time.

KV cache and session considerations:
- Pre-seed KV cache on standby region if traffic shift expected >20%: run prefix prewarm job (see prewarm checklist below).
- If session affinity required, prefer sticky cookies at LB layer and failover to region-b cookie mapping only after user-level retry. Document caveats for long-running streams.

Prewarm checklist (quick actions for ops):
- kick off kv-prewarm job: run with sample of hottest prefixes from the past 2 hours (Linear RED-567). Monitor prewarm completion metric.
- Push read-only model snapshot to standby nodes if model weights not already present. Confirm model version hash matches production.
- Warm GPU kernels & caches with smoke-generation at small qps (0.5–2 rps per instance) to populate KV and compilation caches.
- Confirm binary/infra versions identical across regions (infra/pkgs check).

Observability: what to watch during/after shift (minimum):
- 5xx rate (region-level + global aggregated) — 1m/5m windows
- 95/99/99.9 latency percentiles for token-generation and control-plane ops
- In-flight request count and queue depth (indicates overload)
- KV cache hit-rate and backend miss storms
- Error taxonomy: ratio of upstream failures vs internal infra failures (helps rollback decisions)
- Cloud provider BGP/route-change alerts if available
- Alert if region-b 5xx > 2% or latency 95th > 2x baseline for two consecutive 5m windows

Rollout pattern (example safe plan for full switchover):
- Step 0: Prepare (notify stakeholders, prewarm caches)
- Step 1: Shift 10% weights to standby (2 minutes wait)
- Step 2: Observe 5m (if OK, step 3). If not OK, rollback to 0 and investigate.
- Step 3: Shift to 30% (2m wait), observe 10m
- Step 4: Shift to 60% (2m wait), observe 15m
- Step 5: Shift to 100% and mark region-a degraded and open incident follow-up ticket
- After reaching 100%: maintain cooldown of 60m before allowing any automatic rebalancing

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback):
- New-target region 5xx > 2% sustained 5m post-change
- Tail latency 95th > 3x baseline after weight step and not improving in 10m
- Backend error patterns (e.g., DB connection saturations) appear in the new-primary region

On-call quick play (first 20m summary):
- 0–2m: Confirm validity of metrics (no aggregator flapping). Open decision log entry.
- 2–10m: Execute small weight shift, start prewarm, post message to #sre-ops and #incidents.
- 10–20m: Reassess. If stable, continue planned steps. If unstable, rollback and escalate to infra eng leads.

Communication checklist:
- Post shift intent & progress to #incidents and the affected region's support channel.
- Broadcast to customer-success if any customer-facing degradation expected.
- Create incident ticket with tags: region-switchover, kv-cache, postmortem-needed.

Post-incident follow-ups / action items (example placeholders):
- RED-345: Improve prewarm job scheduling (owner: Samir)
- RED-346: Add cooldown gate to automated failover engine (owner: Riley)
- RED-347: Add per-region DNS TTL audit and automated guardrails (owner: Anika)

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- TTL economics: what is the acceptable minimum DNS TTL for partner/provider combos? (need to test across GCP/OCI/AWS)
- Can we detect a provider-induced BGP flap faster than our app-level probes? Should that be an immediate switchover trigger?
- How do we handle long-lived streamed connections during a gradual weight shift? (Current approach: let existing streams finish, new connections follow weights)

Appendix: quick command snippets (ops cheatsheet)
- Check region health summary (internal tool): /bin/region-health --region region-a --window 10m
- Adjust LB weights (example): infractl lb set-weight --pool production --region region-b --weight 30
- Kick prewarm job: infractl jobs run kv-prewarm --sample 2h --target-region region-b --concurrency 8

Notes to self: keep this short, actionable. This doc is intentionally informal: copy critical parts into a formal playbook after the next two incidents where it’s exercised.

End of sketch.
